options.plan: Free; security offer documented, account entitlement unverified

options.configuration: Local browser customers; hosted MFA/passkeys and OIDC reauthentication; no broker; journey/key assurance unverified

conditions: Select local browser customers using hosted login, configured MFA methods and passkeys; this is not native/mobile, brokered workforce or machine authentication.

The login policy offers Force MFA and local-only enforcement; enabling a method alone is not mandatory use. Passkeys require the U2F-with-PIN option. TOTP, email and SMS are weaker alternatives, not equivalent phishing resistance.

Effective organization settings can override instance defaults; inspect the selected context before relying on enforcement. API examples are not observed account settings: https://zitadel.com/docs/reference/api/settings/zitadel.settings.v2.SettingsService.GetLoginSettings.

The public Free offer advertises all security features and 100 daily active users: https://zitadel.com/pricing. Account entitlement, quotas, deployed version, email/SMS delivery costs and future zero-cost operation are unverified. No subscription, account or provider calls occurred.

evidence.summary: The settings guide documents configurable MFA methods, local-only enforcement and passkey prerequisites. OPTIONAL describes a documented mechanism, not verified compulsory use or Free-account entitlement.

conditions: Availability is a conditional mechanism-level inference from the hosted FIDO2/WebAuthn passkey flow, not all MFA or every login. Bind the intended HTTPS login domain/RP and test browser/authenticator behavior. Protocol context: https://www.w3.org/TR/webauthn-2/.

Password fallback can remain available. Force MFA alone does not establish passkey-only authentication or safe enrollment, password reset, recovery, credential removal, existing SSO and administrator paths. Complete journey enforcement remains UNKNOWN.

The hosted-login guide lists initial Login V2 setup limitations, while https://zitadel.com/docs/guides/integrate/login-ui/login-app lists passkey/U2F setup. Record this source discrepancy; do not infer a deployed Cloud version or automatically resolve it as verified support.

Login and management-console domains affect existing credentials and enrollment. No native, external-IdP, employee, hardware-key or AAL assurance is inherited. The seven earlier ZITADEL scopes, AuthWeave's ZITADEL/BFF and synthetic evaluator are unchanged.

evidence.summary: The hosted-login guide documents FIDO2/WebAuthn passkeys and password fallback. Mechanism availability is conditional; complete customer-journey enforcement is UNKNOWN, including version/domain-dependent setup.

conditions: The custom-browser passkey guide allows platform or cross-platform authenticators and gives iCloud Keychain among credential examples. A passkey label, fingerprint, cross-platform selection or successful WebAuthn login does not prove a non-exportable private key.

The registration example uses attestation none and required user verification; an example is not verified Cloud configuration. Attachment and user verification do not establish hardware key protection. Trusted authenticator evidence and an enforceable enrollment policy remain unverified.

Synced, cross-device, existing credential and recovery paths need independent key-protection review. The custom-UI API is context only, not proof of hosted-login Free entitlement or a hardware-only policy. Keep availability and enforcement UNKNOWN, not provider-wide UNSUPPORTED.

No custom login implementation, security-key purchase, hardware enrollment, attestation verification or physical-device test occurred. Storage countries, SCIM, organization access and machine-key custody are not inferred.

evidence.summary: The custom-browser guide shows authenticator choices, example attestation none and diverse credential examples. It does not verify non-exportability or its enforcement for this selected Cloud hosted-login customer scope.

conditions: The authorization endpoint documents max_age and prompt=login for reauthentication. AuthWeave step-up means requesting and verifying stronger authentication, not repeating the same login. These parameters alone do not establish that capability; availability remains UNKNOWN.

Login lifetimes are separate password, external-login, second-factor and multifactor checks: https://zitadel.com/docs/guides/manage/console/default-settings. A prompt, token refresh, organization-selection scope or a cached SSO session is not proof of a new stronger-factor challenge.

Before a sensitive operation, the application must independently validate signed token issuer/audience/nonce and applicable auth_time, assurance claims and factor freshness; absent or insufficient evidence must deny the operation. This is a required application condition, not a claim that this catalog draft implements it.

Selected documentation does not establish an essential-ACR higher-assurance contract or complete operation gating for the deployed Free login. Enforcement stays UNKNOWN pending policy, recovery, SSO-reuse and bypass tests. Do not inherit Keycloak LoA semantics, NIST AAL or external-IdP assurance.

evidence.summary: The authorization endpoint documents max_age and prompt=login, not a verified stronger-authentication contract. Step-up availability and enforcement remain UNKNOWN; ordinary reauthentication is context only.
